test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Why does a paper cup not burn when filled with water and heated?

options.text: The water evaporates and cools the paper
The water absorbs the heat, preventing the paper from reaching its ignition temperature
The paper becomes fireproof when wet
The water creates steam, which extinguishes the flame

solution:
The correct answer is __**The water absorbs the heat, preventing the paper from reaching its ignition temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon is primarily governed by the principles of **heat transfer** and the specific **ignition temperature** of materials.
 
• **Ignition temperature** is defined as the minimum temperature at which a combustible substance catches fire; for ordinary paper, this is approximately **233 degrees Celsius** (451 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• When a paper cup is filled with water, the heat energy supplied by the flame is rapidly conducted through the thin paper to the **water** inside.
 
• Water has an exceptionally high **specific heat capacity**, meaning it can absorb a large amount of thermal energy before its own temperature rises significantly.
 
• As long as there is water present, the heat is used to raise the water temperature or maintain it at the **boiling point of 100 degrees Celsius**.
 
• Because **100 degrees Celsius** is much lower than the paper's ignition threshold, the paper never becomes hot enough to burn.
 
• The process of **conduction** ensures that the paper and water remain in **thermal equilibrium**, effectively cooling the paper surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phase Change and Latent Heat**:

 
 
• Once the water reaches its boiling point, any additional heat supplied is consumed as **latent heat of vaporization** to convert liquid water into steam.
 
• This phase transition happens at a constant temperature of **100 degrees Celsius**, providing a thermal ceiling that protects the paper from charring.
 
 
 
• **The Fire Triangle**:
 
 
• Combustion requires three components: **Fuel**, **Oxygen**, and **Heat** (sufficient to reach the ignition point). By removing the accumulation of heat, the **fire triangle** is broken.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Conductivity**:
 
 
• While paper itself is not a great conductor, its **thickness** is minimal in a cup, allowing heat to pass through it almost instantly into the liquid medium.
